A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved from the main text into v7 Appendix B.

before.justification: V6 reports original Gaussian simulations and empirical analyses of multilingual, image and image-caption representations, including appendix controls and supplementary comparisons.

after.justification: V7 retains these original simulations and empirical representation analyses in its main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The Information Imbalance calculation, representation extraction and token-aggregation procedures are unchanged. The added discussion of applying feature selection to language representations concerns future work.

E1.justification: Both retain the same Gaussian scenarios, Opus Books and WMT17 translations, ImageNet-1k image pairs, Flickr30k image-caption pairs and language coverage. The 100,000-dimensional Gaussian scenario remains in v7 Appendix B.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: CKA, RSA/Spearman and Neighborhood Overlap for synthetic data, and the existing representation-model comparisons, including CLIP. Linear mappings and model stitching are mentioned as prospective comparisons only.

E3.justification: Sampling, sentence filtering, token pooling, layer sweeps and model configurations are retained. The Gaussian sample size remains 2,500, and the existing CLIP 77-token subset control is unchanged.

E4.justification: Token-aggregation and token-distance analyses, shuffled-pair controls, cross-layer comparisons, language correlations and vision-size/layer controls are retained. V7 Appendix B relocates the existing Gaussian metric comparison rather than introducing another analysis.

E5.justification: Gaussian plots retain standard errors over ten jackknife repetitions. The reported five half-sample resamplings and standard deviations for representation analyses, together with Pearson correlations, permutation testing and Chinese-outlier treatment, are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched plots and numerical results are unchanged, including minimum II of approximately 0.10 for DeepSeek-V3 to DinoV2 and 0.25 for CLIP in Figure 6. V7 Figure 7 redisplays v6 Figure 1b–c with the same curves and uncertainty bands.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 retains the same rank-based Information Imbalance definition. Appendix A retains the copula formulation, restricted mutual information and associated bound without a new derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows English's predictive advantage to the tested language pool and the DeepSeek-V3 comparison to English inputs. The conclusion specifies the languages and second-half layers supporting the English claim and describes the model comparison as one case. The central convergence contribution remains.

C2.justification: V7 explicitly treats online presence as a rough training-exposure proxy and distinguishes correlation from causation. Appendices F and G add substantive qualifications about two-model coverage and the small number of non-Indo-European languages available for inference.

D1.justification: Data sources, filtering instructions, model specifications and aggregation/layer settings remain documented at the same level. No implementation resources or code/data access changes are reported; the added OpenReview link identifies the review record.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Related Work subsection are unchanged. The conclusion adds a limited connection between planned language-feature selection and already cited feature-selection/arrow-of-time research, while it and Appendix F explicitly position future comparisons against linear mappings and model stitching.

P1.justification: The abstract, conclusion and selected interpretive passages receive targeted rewrites. The detailed Gaussian comparison moves from Section 2.3 into a new Appendix B, with corresponding renumbering, publication/review metadata and small copyedits.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a larger two-panel display. Its former high-dimensional panel moves to Figure 7 alongside a repeated 100-dimensional panel and a revised legend. Other figures are retained, with renumbering and page reflow accompanying the publication header.

improvement.justification: V7's narrower abstract and conclusion better match the tested cases. Explicit qualifications about causality, the training-exposure proxy and limited language/model coverage improve interpretive precision. The Gaussian benchmark and other supporting evidence remain available, making this a limited improvement in clarity and transparency.
